Context/Background:
We leverage a clinical trial that compared neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 (Nivo), anti-PD-1+CTLA-4 (Nivo+Ipi), and anti-PD-1+LAG-3 (Nivo+Rela) therapies in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients. Combination therapies promote higher pathologic response rates versus monotherapy, and major pathologic response is associated with better survival. To address whether successful immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) regimens act through similar or distinct pathways, we robustly and longitudinally characterize transcriptional and proteomic dynamics of CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in a clonal manner. 

Thirty-eight patients were evaluable for pathologic tumor response (pTR) and categorized into three groups following previous studies: pTR-0 (91–100% viable residual tumor), pTR-1 (51%–90% viable residual tumor), and pTR-2 (≤50% viable residual tumor. 

To study the association between transcriptional dynamics of T cells and pathologic responses to neoadjuvant ICI treatments, we isolated and profiled 372,914 CD45+CD3+ TIL from 35 patients (29 baseline and 31 post-surgical fresh tumor specimens; 20 patients having matched pre- and post-treatment biopsies), using the 10x Genomics 5′ scRNA-seq workflow. These cells were clustered into five distinct populations annotated as CD8+ T, CD4+ T, FOXP3+ T, γδ T/MAIT and cycling T cell clusters, and visualized by Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) analysis. Clusters were annotated based on the expression of reported canonical T cell marker gene and CITE-seq expression levels.
Prompt:
We analyzed the clusters of CD3+ TIL and found that the proportion of baseline CD8+ TIL showed a trend to the more frequent in responding patients.  When we assessed baseline expression of PDCD1, CTLA4, and LAG3 by CD8+ TIL, we observed the highest expression for PDCD1 and LAG3. The expression of PDCD1 and LAG3 by baseline CD8+ TIL positively correlated with the degree of pathologic response only in Nivo+Rela-treated patients. Similar analyses did not show a significant correlation between LAG3, PDCD1 and CTLA4 expression levels in baseline CD8+ TIL and the degree of pathologic response in the Nivo and Nivo+Ipi cohorts.

To identify baseline CD8+ TIL transcriptional signatures correlating with pathologic response, we generated a list of differentially expressed genes (DEG) between pTR-2 and pTR-0 tumors for each regimen.

Based on the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between pTR-2 and pTR-0 tumors for the Nivo+Ipi and Nivo+Rela cohorts, generate a summary describing the key transcriptional signatures, functional categories, and immune pathways enriched in pTR-2 vs pTR-0 tumors. Highlight representative genes and link them to their biological roles.  Focus on T cell–specific functional programs and gene modules defined by known immune states.

Introduction/Context  
A neoadjuvant clinical trial in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma compared anti–PD-1 monotherapy (Nivo), anti–PD-1+CTLA-4 (Nivo+Ipi), and anti–PD-1+LAG-3 (Nivo+Rela). Single-cell RNA-seq of baseline CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between major responders (pTR-2, ≤50% viable tumor) versus non-responders (pTR-0, 91–100% viable tumor) under each regimen. Two DEG lists were profiled: one for Nivo+Rela (baseline_Nivo_Rela.csv; 983 genes) and one for Nivo+Ipi (baseline_Nivo_Ipi.csv; 998 genes). Definitive signals in Nivo+Rela responders point to interferon-driven and T cell–activation modules, whereas Nivo+Ipi responders exhibit metabolic and translational programs.

Keywords  
• Interferon signaling  
• Translation/ribosome  
• T cell activation  
• Metabolism/oxidative phosphorylation  
• Immune checkpoint molecules  

Candidate Genes  
MX1, STAT1, IFI44L, ISG15, CXCL13, LAG3, CTLA4, COX5B  

Pathway Enrichments  

1. Nivo+Rela (pTR-2 vs pTR-0)  
– MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (Up)  
  • Interferon Gamma Response (NES 5.55 FDR 1.2e-6) ⇒ MX1, STAT1, IFI44L, ISG15, CD38, EPSTI1  
  • Interferon Alpha Response (NES 4.26 FDR 4.1e-4) ⇒ MX1, IFI44L, ISG15, OAS1, RSAD2  
  • Allograft Rejection (NES 4.23 FDR 4.7e-23) ⇒ CXCL13, PRF1, GZMA, GZMB, LCK  

– MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (Down)  
  • Hypoxia (NES –2.19 FDR 0.21) ⇒ CXCR4, FOS, DUSP1, ZFP36  

– GO_Biological_Process_2023 (Up)  
  • Defense Response To Virus (NES 4.56 p 5e-6) ⇒ OAS1, IFIT1, RSAD2, IRF1, APOBEC3G  
  • Positive Regulation Of CD8+ T Cell Activation (GO:2001187; NES ?) ⇒ NCKAP1L, PTPN22, RUNX3, HLA-A  
  • T Cell Receptor Signaling (GO:0050852; NES ?) ⇒ CTLA4, ITK, PTPN22, LCP2, CD247  

– GO_Biological_Process_2023 (Down)  
  • Peptide Biosynthetic Process (NES –3.79 p 1.5e-4) ⇒ RPS18, RPL36, RPS28, RPS13  
  • Translation (NES –3.67 p 2.4e-4) ⇒ RPS18, RPL36, EEF1B2, RPL30  

2. Nivo+Ipi (pTR-2 vs pTR-0)  
– MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (Up)  
  • Oxidative Phosphorylation (NES 3.93 FDR 0.0033) ⇒ COX4I1, COX5B, ATP5MC2, UQCRB  
  • Myc Targets V1 (NES 3.37 FDR 0.015) ⇒ RPL6, RPS5, RPL22, EEF1B2  

– MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (Down)  
  • UV Response DN (NES –3.18 FDR 0.019) ⇒ RUNX1, PTEN, FYN  
  • Estrogen Response Early (NES –2.92 FDR 0.034) ⇒ IL6ST, FKBP5  

– GO_Biological_Process_2023 (Up)  
  • Cytoplasmic Translation (NES 6.15 FDR 2.4e-7) ⇒ RPS26, RPL30, RPS5, RPS15A  
  • Peptide Biosynthetic Process (NES 6.09 FDR 2.4e-7) ⇒ RPS23, RPS9, RPL27, RPS14  

– GO_Biological_Process_2023 (Down)  
  • Regulation Of Transcription By RNA Pol II (NES –∞ FDR 0) ⇒ FOXP1, RUNX1, ETS1, TOX  

Analysis  
In the Nivo+Rela cohort, pTR-2 CD8+ TILs are skewed toward potent interferon-driven antiviral-like and TCR-activation programs, with upregulated ISGs (MX1, ISG15, OAS1) and checkpoint/activation markers (LAG3, CTLA4, CD38). Concurrent downregulation of ribosomal/translation pathways suggests a shift from basal protein synthesis toward effector differentiation. By contrast, Nivo+Ipi responders show enrichment of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and Myc-driven proliferation modules, coupled with broad activation of translation machinery—indicative of a metabolically primed, high-output state. These divergent transcriptional states—effector-biased interferon imprinting under LAG-3 blockade versus metabolic/biogenic priming under CTLA-4 blockade—highlight distinct routes to effective T cell–mediated tumor clearance.  

Representative Genes & Roles  
• MX1 (Up, Nivo+Rela): interferon-induced antiviral GTPase; marks IFN-γ activation.  
• STAT1 (Up, Nivo+Rela): central transcription factor in Type I/II IFN signaling.  
• IFIT1/ISG15 (Up, both): innate-immune effectors inhibiting viral replication.  
• COX5B (Up, Nivo+Ipi): mitochondrial electron-transport chain; supports high OXPHOS.  
• RPS26/RPL30 (Up, Nivo+Ipi): ribosomal proteins driving increased translation.  
• CTLA4 (Up, Nivo+Rela): inhibitory receptor; part of TCR-signaling enrichment.  

Implications  
These regimen-specific TIL states suggest that LAG-3 combination promotes an antiviral-like, interferon-skewed effector phenotype, whereas CTLA-4 addition yields a proliferative, metabolically active TIL pool. Tailoring ICI combinations to harness these distinct states may optimize durable responses.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
• Validate post-treatment TIL states by scRNA-seq to confirm sustained module activation.  
• Functionally assay cytotoxicity and proliferation in vitro for interferon-high versus OXPHOS-high TILs.  
• Investigate co-expression of metabolic and checkpoint markers (e.g., LAG3 vs. COX5B) by CITE-seq.  
• Explore whether translation downregulation in Nivo+Rela responders confers stress resistance.

References  
None.
